rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Makes it unlawful, and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act, for a rental property owner or its agents to pay for or use the services of a coordinator, meaning a person operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function. It is also unlawful for a coordinator to facilitate agreements among rental property owners that restrict competition, for any person to engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination, and for any person to perform a coordinating function.

coverage_conditions.text: Rental property owners (persons owning, directly or indirectly, one or more rental residential dwelling units), their agents, representatives and subcontractors, coordinators, and any person. Residential dwelling units are any house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended to be used as a primary residence in the State.

rules.exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. An algorithmic device excludes a spreadsheet that operates without artificial intelligence and requires human analysis, and a database that only uses an algorithm to query unprocessed data stored in it. A coordinating function excludes using competitively sensitive information solely for research, statistical analysis or testing not used to set or recommend rents or lease terms; developing a rent estimate made available to the public at no cost; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms to subscribers that do not set or recommend prices or collect competitively sensitive information to do so; and a government entity setting or limiting rents through affordability controls. rules.title: Prohibition on sale of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Prohibits selling, licensing, or otherwise providing to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: Anyone who sells, licenses, or provides coordinated pricing algorithms (processes using nonpublic Competitor Data less than 90 days old to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and competitors) to City of Berkeley landlords.
rules.exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines of a government; and products or processes for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing, or training for software development (if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated).
rules.quoted_span:

landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.penalty: City Attorney may file a civil action for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; court shall award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to the City Attorney if prevailing.

rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not end a tenancy without just cause. Allowed at-fault causes include failure to pay rent, uncured lease violations, nuisance or damage, illegal use, refusing to renew a similar agreement, denying reasonable access, and an unapproved subtenant at lease end. No-fault causes (owner or family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, government order to vacate, HUD sale, residential hotel conversion, conversion to affordable housing) may require relocation assistance.

coverage_conditions.text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and properties with only one single-family dwelling. rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term treatment centers for substance abuse, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government. At-fault evictions carry no relocation assistance.
